paper.title: Provable Model-based Nonlinear Bandit and Reinforcement Learning: Shelve Optimism, Embrace Virtual Curvature

settings.name_in_paper: Nonlinear bandit problem with deterministic reward
unmapped: continuous actions in R^{d_A}, deterministic reward eta(theta*, a) in [0,1] with realizable parameterized class
reward gradient/Hessian bounded and Hessian Lipschitz (zeta_g, zeta_h, zeta_3rd), known to the algorithm
regret measured against the worst (eps_g, eps_h)-approximate local maximum (local regret)
algorithm may query infinitesimal finite differences (several actions per round) to estimate directional gradients/Hessians
settings.definition_quote: We consider deterministic nonlinear bandit problem with continuous actions. Let $\theta \in \Theta$ be the parameter that specifies the bandit instance, $a\in \R^{\da}$ the action, and $\eta(\theta,a)\in [0,1]$ the reward function... we work under the realizability assumption that $\thetas\in \Theta.$

settings.name_in_paper: Model-based RL with deterministic dynamics and stochastic policies
unmapped: finite-horizon deterministic dynamics class, parameterized stochastic policies, trajectory observations
settings.definition_quote: We consider finite horizon Markov decision process (MDP) with deterministic dynamics, defined by a tuple $\left<\dy,r,H,\mu_1\right>$...

settings.name_in_paper: One-layer ReLU neural net bandit with deterministic reward (global optimum)
settings.definition_quote: the reward function can be written in the form of $\eta((w,b),a)=\mathrm{ReLU}(\dotp{w}{a}+b).$

settings.name_in_paper: Deterministic linear ground truth on the sphere with two-layer NN hypothesis (UCB lower bound)

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear bandit with Gaussian noise, finding local maxima (lower bound)
unmapped: goal: find a (0.1,1)-approximate second order stationary point
settings.definition_quote: Our hard instance is linear bandit with hypothesis $\Theta=\{e_1,\cdots,e_d\}$, action space $\calA=S^{d-1}$ and i.i.d. standard Gaussian noise.

symbols.R_T: sequential Rademacher complexity of the loss class in Eq. (bandit-loss)
symbols.zeta_h: bound on reward Hessian spectral norm

conditions: Assumption 2.1 (bounded gradient/Hessian, Lipschitz Hessian)
realizability theta* in Theta
deterministic reward
regret is (epsilon, 6 sqrt(zeta_3 epsilon))-local regret

source.label: thm:bandit-main
source.quote: Let $\src_T$ be the sequential Rademacher complexity of the family of the losses defined in Eq.~\eqref{equ:bandit-loss}. Let $C_1=2+\gasup/\hasup$. Under Assumption~\ref{assumption:lipschitz}, for any $\epsilon\le \mintwo{1}{\tasup/16},$ we can bound the $(\epsilon,6\sqrt{\tasup\epsilon})$-local regret of Alg.~\ref{alg:ban} from above by $\E[\reg_{\epsilon,6\sqrt{\tasup\epsilon}}(T)]\le (1+C_1\sqrt{4T\src_T})\max(4\hasup\epsilon^{-2},\sqrt{\tasup}\epsilon^{-3/2})$.

results.notes: Local regret against worst approximate local maximum; quantity 'other'. Algorithm's maximization step may be computationally hard (not stated).

symbols.R_Theta: complexity parameter such that sequential Rademacher complexity <= sqrt(R(Theta) T polylog T)

conditions: sequential Rademacher complexity of loss bounded by sqrt(R(Theta) T polylog(T))
Assumption 2.1
success probability 0.5 of finding an (epsilon, 6 sqrt(zeta_3 epsilon))-approximate local maximum action

source.label: thm:ban-action-space
source.quote: Suppose the sequential Rademacher complexity of the loss function (defined in Eq.~\eqref{equ:bandit-loss}) is bounded by $\sqrt{R(\Theta)T\polylog(T)}.$ When $T\gtrsim R(\Theta)\epsilon^{-8}\polylog(R(\Theta),1/\epsilon)$, if we run Alg.~\ref{alg:ban} for $T$ steps, there exists $t\in [T]$ such that $a_t\in \sosp_{\epsilon,6\sqrt{\tasup\epsilon}}$ with probability at least $0.5$.

results.notes: Probability is a constant 0.5, not 1-delta; zeta constants treated as constants.

conditions: two-layer neural net reward eta((W1,W2),a)=W2 sigma(W1 a) (regularized by -||a||^2/2)
activation satisfies Assumption B.2 (bounded derivatives up to 2nd order, Lipschitz second derivative)

source.label: thm:two-layer
source.quote: Let $\Theta=\{(W_1,W_2):\normone{\mW_2}\le 1,\norm{\mW_1}_{1,\infty}\le 1\}$ be the parameter hypothesis. Under the setting of Theorem~\ref{thm:bandit-main} with Assumption~\ref{assumption:two-layer}, the local regret of Alg.~\ref{alg:ban} running on two-layer neural networks can be bounded by $\tildeO\pbra{\epsilon^{-2}T^{3/4}}.$

conditions: two-layer neural net reward with ||W2||_1 <= 1, ||W1||_{1,inf} <= 1, Assumption B.2
network is input concave (reward concave in action)

source.label: thm:two-layer
source.quote: In addition, if the neural network is input concave, then the global regret of Alg.~\ref{alg:ban} is bounded by $\tildeO\pbra{T^{7/8}}.$

results.notes: Global regret of the regularized reward per the proof; deterministic reward so expectation over algorithm randomness only.

symbols.R_T_dyn: sequential Rademacher complexity of the l2 dynamics loss in Eq. (rl-loss)
symbols.zeta_h: bound on Hessian of return w.r.t. policy parameters
symbols.zeta_3: Lipschitz constant of Hessian of return

conditions: Assumptions 2.1, 4.1, 4.2
deterministic dynamics and reward, stochastic policies, realizability

source.label: thm:rl-main
source.quote: Let $c_1=HL_0^2(4H^2\Ph+4H^4\Pt+2H^2\Pg+1)+HL_1^2(8H^2\Pg+2)+4HL_2^2$ and $C_1=2+\frac{\gasup}{\hasup}$. ... for any $\epsilon\le \mintwo{1}{\frac{\tasup}{16}},$ we can bound the $(\epsilon,6\sqrt{\tasup\epsilon})$-regret of Alg.~\ref{alg:rl} by $\E[\reg(T)]\le (1+C_1\sqrt{2c_1T\srcrl_T})\max(2\hasup\epsilon^{-2},\sqrt{\tasup}\epsilon^{-3/2})$.

conditions: one-layer ReLU network reward class
deterministic reward, actions in unit ball

source.label: thm:lowerbound-sample-comp
source.quote: When the function class is chosen to be one-layer neural networks with ReLU activation, the minimax sample complexity is $\Omega(\varepsilon^{-(d-2)}).$

results.notes: Proof goes via minimax regret Omega(T^{(d-2)/(d-1)}) and sample-complexity reduction.

conditions: applies to the UCB algorithm with the tightest upper confidence bound in deterministic environments
sample complexity for finding a (31/2048)-suboptimal action

source.label: thm:lowerbound-optimism
source.quote: Consider the case where the ground-truth reward function is linear: $\dotp{\thetas}{a}$ and the action set is $a\in S^{d-1}.$ If the hypothesis is chosen to be two-layer neural network with width $d$, UCB algorithm with tightest upper confidence bound suffers exponential sample complexity .

results.notes: Statement says 'exponential'; Omega(2^d) taken from the proof.

conditions: hypothesis class {e_1,...,e_d} with log|Theta| = O~(1)
standard Gaussian noise (sigma = 1)
goal: (0.1,1)-approximate second order stationary point with probability at least 3/4

source.label: thm:lowerbound-stochastic
source.quote: There exists an bandit problem with stochastic reward and hypothesis class with size $\log |\Theta|=\tildeO\pbra{1}$, such that any algorithm requires $\Omega\pbra{d}$ sample to find a $(0.1,1)$-approximate second order stationary point with probability at least $3/4.$
